paper.title: Honor Among Bandits: No-Regret Learning for Online Fair Division

settings.name_in_paper: Online fair division with unknown values under envy-freeness in expectation (EFE)
unmapped: Arms are (player, item type) pairs; n players and m item types; item type k_t drawn uniformly (known distribution) each round and the learner commits to a fractional allocation (distribution over players per type) before observing k_t
Fairness constraint: envy-freeness in expectation w.r.t. the unknown mean matrix must hold at every round with probability 1-1/T
Means bounded in [a,b] with a>0 known to the learner
Regret measured against the optimal constrained fractional allocation Y^{mu*} (LP solution)
settings.definition_quote: At each time step $t \in [T]$, an item $j_t$ of type $k_t$ arrives, where $k_t \sim \mathcal{D}$ ... The algorithm observes the item type $k_t$, and must then immediately allocate the item $j_t$ to a player $i_t$, at which time the algorithm observes that player's value $V_{i_t}(j_t)$. ... $\alg$ satisfies envy-freeness in expectation ($\efe$) if for all $t$ and all $H_t$, $ (X_t)_i \cdot \mu^*_i \ge \max_{i' \in [n]} (X_t)_{i'} \cdot \mu^*_i$ for all $i$.

settings.name_in_paper: Online fair division with unknown values under proportionality in expectation (PE)
unmapped: Arms are (player, item type) pairs; n players and m item types; item type drawn uniformly each round; learner commits to a fractional allocation before seeing the type
Fairness constraint: proportionality in expectation w.r.t. unknown means must hold at every round with probability 1-1/T
Means bounded in [a,b] with a>0 known to the learner
Regret measured against the optimal constrained fractional allocation
settings.definition_quote: $\alg$ satisfies proportionality in expectation ($\pexp$) if for all $t$ and all histories $H_t$, $(X_t)_i \cdot \mu^*_i \ge \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i' \in [n]} (X_t)_{i'} \cdot \mu^*_i$ for all $i$.

settings.name_in_paper: Online fair division under envy-freeness in expectation (lower bound)
unmapped: Arms are (player, item type) pairs; item type drawn uniformly each round
Fairness constraint (envy-freeness in expectation, equivalently proportionality for n=2) must hold every round w.p. 1-1/T
settings.definition_quote: Let $a = 1$, $b = 3$, $n = 2$, and $m = 2$, and assume that the distributions of values are all normal distributions with variance $1$. For $n=2$, envy-freeness and proportionality are equivalent

settings.name_in_paper: Online fair division under proportionality in expectation (lower bound)
unmapped: Arms are (player, item type) pairs; item type drawn uniformly each round
Proportionality in expectation must hold every round w.p. 1-1/T
settings.definition_quote: The same is true for the proportionality constraints.

settings.name_in_paper: Online fair division with means not bounded away from zero
unmapped: Means allowed anywhere in [0, eps] (not bounded away from zero)
Envy-freeness or proportionality in expectation must hold every round with probability > 1/2
settings.definition_quote: For $\epsilon > 0$, there does not exist an algorithm $\alg$ such that for any possible $\mu^* \in [0,\epsilon]^{n \times m}$, for every $t$ the fractional allocation $X_t$ chosen by $\alg$ satisfies envy-freeness in expectation with probability greater than $1/2$ and the regret of $\alg$ is $o(T)$.

conditions: 0 < a <= mu*_{ik} <= b for all i,k
sub-Gaussian values, item types uniform over [m]
tuning: exploration length T^{2/3} with uniform-at-random allocation

source.label: thm:23foref
source.quote: Suppose we are given $n,m, T, a,b$ such that $0 < a \le \mu^*_{ik} \le b$ ... If $\{\{(B_\ell(\mu), c_\ell)\}_{\ell=1}^{L}\}_{\mu} = \{\efeconst(\mu)\}_{\mu}$ or ... $\{\pexpconst(\mu)\}_{\mu}$, then Algorithm \ref{algo:ETC} with probability $1-1/T$ satisfies the constraints ... and achieves regret of $\tilde{O}(T^{2/3})$

results.notes: Holds with probability 1-1/T jointly with constraint satisfaction. Õ hides constants depending on n, m, a, b (exponential in n for EF). Regret defined via means of fractional allocations. LP is semi-infinite; paper says it can be solved in poly time via ellipsoid with separation oracle.

conditions: 0 < a <= mu*_{ik} <= b for all i,k
sub-Gaussian values, item types uniform over [m]
tuning: exploration length T^{2/3} with uniform-at-random allocation

source.label: thm:23foref
source.quote: ... or $\{\{(B_\ell(\mu), c_\ell)\}_{\ell=1}^{L}\}_{\mu} = \{\pexpconst(\mu)\}_{\mu}$, then Algorithm \ref{algo:ETC} with probability $1-1/T$ satisfies the constraints ... and achieves regret of $\tilde{O}(T^{2/3})$

results.notes: Proportionality case of Theorem 1; constants polynomial in n per discussion.

conditions: algorithms that satisfy the envy-freeness in expectation constraints for all t with probability at least 1-1/T
instance: n=2, m=2, a=1, b=3, Gaussian values with variance 1

source.label: thm:lower_bounds
source.quote: There exists $a,b,n,m$ such that no algorithm can, for all $\mu^* \in [a,b]^{n \times m}$, both satisfy the envy-freeness constraints and achieve regret of less than $\frac{T^{2/3}}{\log(T)}$ with probability at least $1-1/T$. The same is true for the proportionality constraints.

results.notes: Impossibility: no algorithm can, w.p. >= 1-1/T, both satisfy EF constraints and have regret < T^{2/3}/log T for all instances. Recorded as Omega.

conditions: algorithms that satisfy the proportionality in expectation constraints for all t with probability at least 1-1/T
instance: n=2, m=2, a=1, b=3, Gaussian values with variance 1

source.label: thm:lower_bounds
source.quote: The same is true for the proportionality constraints.

results.notes: Proportionality case of Theorem 2 (equivalent to EF for n=2).

conditions: algorithms that satisfy envy-freeness (or proportionality) in expectation at every t with probability greater than 1/2
means in [0, eps]^{n x m}, Bernoulli values, n=2, m=2, T>=2

source.label: thm:bounded_from_0
source.quote: For $\epsilon > 0$, there does not exist an algorithm $\alg$ such that for any possible $\mu^* \in [0,\epsilon]^{n \times m}$, for every $t$ the fractional allocation $X_t$ chosen by $\alg$ satisfies envy-freeness in expectation with probability greater than $1/2$ and the regret of $\alg$ is $o(T)$. The same result also holds for proportionality in expectation.

results.notes: Stated as impossibility of o(T) regret; recorded as Omega(T). Applies to both EF and PE.
